### You Shall Be Clean
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-april-7-2024.html
Passage: 2 Kings 5:10-11
Points:
- Naaman held high status and wealth, yet neither power nor royal connections could cure his condition.
- Elisha’s command to wash in the Jordan offended Naaman because it was simple and lacked flattering spectacle.
- Leprosy illustrates the devastating reality of human sin, which cannot be solved by human effort.
- Cleansing requires humbling oneself and receiving the cure accomplished through Christ on the cross.

### An Unlikely Hero
Author: Heather Bleier
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement-cafe/an-unlikely-hero-encouragement-caf-january-29-2016.html
Passage: 2 Kings 5:2-3
Points:
- Despite being an esteemed military leader, Naaman was helpless against an incurable, rotting affliction.
- God chose an unnamed young Israelite girl held in foreign captivity to reveal the path to healing.
- Instead of yielding to anger or despair over her bondage, she spoke faithfully about the true God.
- Believers experiencing trials are empowered by the Holy Spirit to point others to Christ.

### Demonstrations of Power
Author: Ken Jones
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/demonstrations-of-power
Passage: 2 Kings 5:11-12
Points:
- Naaman became angry because he expected a grand theatrical performance instead of a mundane instruction.
- Human nature frequently craves spectacular sensations and equates showy displays with genuine spiritual authority.
- Unlike Naaman, the Roman centurion in Matthew 8 understood that God's power operates through a simple word.
- God regularly conveys His redemptive grace through humble, ordinary means rather than flashy demonstrations.

### The Unimpressive Path to Immortality
Author: Greg Morse
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/the-unimpressive-path-to-immortality
Passage: 2 Kings 5:13
Points:
- Naaman would eagerly have undertaken a heroic quest, but despised an unglamorous dip in the river.
- His servants prompted him to see that restoration demanded surrendering his pride to simple obedience.
- Many reject salvation because trusting a crucified Savior seems unimpressive to human wisdom.
- Enduring spiritual life is sustained not through theatrics, but through ordinary habits of prayer and Scripture.
